Hi Derek,

I'm reaching out to you personally because we've encountered a significant scheduling overlap that affects your booking for the weekend of October 12th. Due to a synchronization error between our third-party booking platform and our internal management software, the "Evergreen Suite" you reserved was inadvertently double-booked for a wedding party that finalized their contract several months ago.

We understand that you chose our boutique hotel specifically for your tenth anniversary because of the suite's private balcony and view of the lighthouse. Unfortunately, as we are a small heritage property, we do not have an identical room available during that timeframe. To rectify this situation, we would like to offer you a complimentary "lateral transfer" to our sister property, The Obsidian Pier, which is located just three blocks away.

While The Obsidian is a more modern, industrial-style hotel, we have set aside their "Penthouse Studio" for you. This room actually features a larger outdoor space than the Evergreen Suite, though the view is of the harbor rather than the lighthouse. To compensate for the frustration this change surely causes, we will not only honor your original, lower rate at the Obsidian but will also include a $150 credit for their Michelin-starred dining room, The Anchor.

Alternatively, if your heart was set on the heritage atmosphere of our hotel, we can move your reservation to the following weekend (October 19th–21st). If you choose this route, the entire three-night stay will be on the house, and we will arrange for a private champagne breakfast to be delivered to your door each morning. Please let us know by Thursday at noon which of these options best suits your plans so we can release the hold on the other rooms. We value your patronage and are committed to making this anniversary memorable despite this technical hiccup.

Sincerely,
Marcus Thorne
General Manager, The Stonebridge Inn
